subject: general
question: What is the frictional force exerted by fluids known as?
solution:
The correct answer is __**Drag**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Drag** is the specific term used in **physics** and **fluid dynamics** to describe the **frictional force** exerted by **fluids** (which include both **liquids** and **gases**) on any object moving through them.
 
• The magnitude of **fluid friction** or **drag** depends on the **speed** of the object relative to the fluid; typically, as the **velocity** increases, the resistive force also increases. ***Hence, the correct answer is Drag.***
 
• Another critical factor determining **drag** is the **shape** of the object. Objects that are **streamlined**, such as **aeroplanes**, **submarines**, and **birds**, are designed to minimize this **frictional force** and reduce **energy loss**.
 
• **Fluid friction** is also influenced by the **nature of the fluid**, specifically its **viscosity**. A highly viscous fluid like **honey** or **glycerin** will exert a much greater **drag** than a less viscous fluid like **water** or **air**.
 
• When an object moves through a **fluid**, it must overcome the **resistance** offered by the fluid particles, which results in the conversion of some **kinetic energy** into **heat energy**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Lift:**

 
 
• **Lift** is a mechanical force generated by a solid object moving through a **fluid**. It acts **perpendicular** to the direction of the flow.
 
• In **aviation**, **lift** is what allows an **aircraft** to overcome **gravity** and stay in the air, usually explained by **Bernoulli's Principle** and **Newton's Third Law of Motion**. ***Hence, statement 1 is incorrect in the context of being the name for frictional force.***
 
 
 
• **Pressure:**
 
 
• **Pressure** is defined as the **force** acting **perpendicularly** on a unit **area** of a surface.
 
• In **fluid mechanics**, it is measured in **Pascals (Pa)**. While fluids exert pressure, it is a scalar quantity and distinct from the resistive frictional force known as **drag**. ***Hence, statement 3 is incorrect.***
 
 
 
• **Load:**
 
 
• A **load** generally refers to the **weight** or the **external force** applied to a structure or component.
 
• In **engineering**, it describes the **mass** or **force** that a system must support, rather than the internal or external **friction** caused by **fluid flow**. ***Hence, statement 4 is incorrect.***
 
 
 
• **Viscosity:**
 
 
• This is a measure of a **fluid's resistance to deformation** or flow. It is often described as the "thickness" of a liquid.
 
• Internal **viscosity** within the fluid layers contributes significantly to the total **drag** experienced by an object. For instance, **engine oil** is designed with specific **viscosity grades** to manage **friction** in **automotive** parts.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Streamlining:** This refers to the process of shaping an object, such as a **car** or **rocket**, to reduce **air resistance** or **water resistance**. **Nature** provides excellent examples of **streamlining** in **dolphins** and **migratory birds** to conserve energy during **long-distance travel**.
 
• **Air Resistance:** This is a specific type of **drag** that acts on objects as they travel through the **atmosphere**. It is a key factor in the **terminal velocity** of falling objects, such as **parachutists**.
 
• **Fluid Friction and Heat:** Just like **solid friction**, **fluid friction** generates **heat**. This is why **spacecraft** entering the **Earth's atmosphere** at high **speeds** require **heat shields** to protect them from the intense heat generated by **atmospheric drag**.
